Which dystopian novel by Ray Bradbury features a society where books are banned and burned?
questions.explanation: Fahrenheit 451, published in 1953, is Ray Bradbury's most celebrated novel, depicting a future America where "firemen" burn books rather than extinguish fires. The title refers to the temperature at which paper supposedly ignites. It remains a landmark of dystopian literature and is widely taught in schools.

questions.question: In Harper Lee's classic novel, what does the title bird symbolize — such that killing one represents the destruction of innocence?
questions.explanation: In Harper Lee's To Kill a Mockingbird, the titular bird is used as a symbol of innocence and goodness. Characters like Tom Robinson and Boo Radley are considered symbolic versions of this bird — harmless beings who are nonetheless harmed by society. The novel won the Pulitzer Prize in 1961 and remains one of the most widely read books in American literature.

questions.question: Which Doris Lessing novel is described as her most experimental work and a study of a woman's psyche and life situation?
questions.explanation: The Golden Notebook (1962) is widely regarded as Doris Lessing's most ambitious and experimental novel, using a fragmented structure of notebooks to explore the inner life of its protagonist, Anna Wulf. It became a landmark text in feminist literature, though Lessing herself had mixed feelings about it being reduced to a feminist manifesto. Lessing went on to win the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2007.

questions.question: Which author originally released The Martian as a self-published blog serial before it became a debut novel in 2011?
questions.explanation: Andy Weir posted The Martian chapter by chapter on his personal blog, where it gained a devoted following before he self-published it as an e-book in 2011. Its viral success caught the attention of publishers, leading to a traditional print deal and eventually a major Hollywood film adaptation starring Matt Damon in 2015.
